items.title: Lillian Hardin Armstrong Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: Mrs. Jones sent them all the men piano players, none of them suited them. So, one night she decided to send me over.

ctx.x: So, when did you get here?

Oh, it was, um, well, we moved here the last part of, uh, 1918. And, um, I was to go back to school the following, uh, September. In the meantime, I went down State Street one day, and I passed this music store, with all this music in the window, so I went in and asked the lady for a song, that I had heard, but I didn't know the name of it, so I hummed it over, and, uh, they had a man there, playing, demonstrating music, and he said, oh, I know what it is, so, he played it, oh, for me, but he didn't play it so…
that's true, no, I was watching, I was watching the volume meter, oh, I see, mm-hmm, I watched the volume meter occasionally,
